phase_name: Tests — push guard, wrapper, exclusions, fail-closed

objectives.description: Register the new test in manifest.json provides.scripts

approaches_tried.approach: Single-use test relying only on HEAD-move/deletion for non-replay
approaches_tried.reason: Re-writing a consumed grant's exact bytes back to disk (with HEAD unchanged) re-created a byte-identical, fully-verifying grant that re-authorized the push -- exposed a real gap: delete-on-use alone is not tamper-independent single-use.

deviations.description: Added a consumed-HMAC ledger (specs/.push-grant/.consumed, append-only) to push-grant-lib.sh beyond what Phase 2 originally specified
deviations.reason: Discovered via this phase's own single-use test (per the research's 'test it directly, not via the sha side door' instruction) that delete-on-use alone fails to prevent replay when the exact grant bytes are restored to disk with HEAD unchanged. Added pg_consumed_ledger_path/pg_hmac_already_consumed/pg_hmac_record_consumed to push-grant-lib.sh (Phase 2's file) and wired them into pg_grant_find_match (skip a match whose HMAC is already in the ledger) and pg_grant_consume (record the HMAC before deleting). This is a genuine strengthening of Phase 2's design, not a Phase 7 scope expansion for its own sake -- the gap was real and reachable outside the tool-call tamper guard (e.g. a stray backup or restore).
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered — added a consumed-HMAC ledger to push-grant-lib.sh to make single-use tamper-independent, not just delete-on-use; see push-grant-lib.sh's pg_hmac_already_consumed/pg_hmac_record_consumed)*

verification_notes: 42/42 cases pass. Fixture self-check first. Non-vacuity proven by disabling the HMAC comparison (sed-patched push-grant-lib.sh temporarily) and confirming exactly one case flips to FAIL, then restoring and confirming 42/42 again. Auto-discovery confirmed: run-all.sh globs scripts/tests/test-*.sh with no registration needed. test-guard-destructive-git.sh re-run: 72/72 still pass unmodified after the ledger addition (it doesn't touch that hook's own logic).
